events.title: Royal Proclamation Draws a Line Across North America
events.description: King George III issued a proclamation that barred British colonists from settling much of the territory Britain had newly won from France. The land was reserved for Indigenous peoples.
events.significance: The proclamation angered many colonists who wanted to move west. It became one of the early grievances that fed tensions leading to the American Revolution.

events.title: Second Battle of Saratoga
events.description: American forces defeated the British at Bemis Heights in New York. This was the second of two decisive engagements fought near Saratoga.
events.significance: The victory is widely seen as a turning point of the American Revolutionary War. It helped persuade France to ally with the American cause.

events.title: Death of Edgar Allan Poe
events.description: The American author and poet died in Baltimore at age 40, after being found in a state of distress a few days earlier. The circumstances of his death remain a mystery.
events.significance: Poe pioneered the modern detective story and shaped the horror and Gothic genres. His works, including 'The Raven' and 'The Tell-Tale Heart,' are still widely read.

events.title: Luna 3 Reveals the Far Side of the Moon
events.description: The Soviet spacecraft Luna 3 took the first photographs of the Moon's far side, which never faces Earth, and sent them back for study.
events.significance: Humanity saw the hidden hemisphere of the Moon for the first time. It was a landmark in space exploration during the early Space Race.

events.title: War in Afghanistan Begins
events.description: US and allied forces launched military strikes in Afghanistan under the name Operation Enduring Freedom. The campaign was part of the response to the September 11 attacks.
events.significance: It opened what became the longest war in US history. It also reshaped global politics and security for two decades.
